question: Which private-equity rivals are most active in our sectors?
html:
Most active private-equity rivals by sector

Residential services is the busiest field. Large-cap consolidators and four sponsor-backed buyers are working in or next to Punctual Pros' counties. Commercial electrical is next, though its institutional roll-ups mostly sit outside CET's New England footprint (Private-equity landscape).

Activity by portfolio company

Portfolio companyMost active rivalsRead
Punctual ProsSila (Goldman Sachs), Legacy/HL Bowman (Gridiron), Ally (Watchtower), Northwinds (TruArc). Nationally: Apex (Alpine), Wrench (LGP), Redwood (Altas), T3 (Riverside)Most crowded. National buyers set add-on pricing
CETKohlberg (RESA Power, Loenbro, CLEAResult); Huron (Criticore, Albireo)Open space in New England for now
FrontlineAlpine's Evergreen, EagleTree/Integreon, BVNo direct sponsor-backed copy yet
Thomas ScientificCalibre ScientificMain bidder for U.S. add-ons

Residential services detail

  • Apex completed 46 add-ons in 2023 and 60 in 2025 (Home-services company case studies).
  • Sila's growth has come almost entirely from acquisitions. Its revenue is est. $450–650M, low confidence (Competitor filings).
  • Not every rival can still bid hard. Horizon pays part of its interest in kind (PIK) and is marked at 92.5. Any Hour (marked 89) and TurnPoint have also moved to PIK. Est.: these are more likely to sell assets than buy (Competitor filings).

Electrical and energy services

  • Since 2023, PE has accounted for most electrical-contractor M&A (Private-equity landscape).
  • The rivals to watch are Albireo's Upstate NY expansion and Kohlberg's energy-efficiency cluster.
  • IES is a public strategic, not a sponsor. It has no net debt and an 11.4% operating margin, so it can pay strategic prices for New England contractors (Competitor filings).

Fund-level thesis peers

  • MidOcean, CIVC, Trilantic North America, Palladium, Vesterra/Comvest and Bertram are the closest thesis-level peers by sector and equity band (Private-equity landscape).
  • Rivals for similar deals often run $0.9–2.1B flagship funds, for example Gridiron V at $2.1B. BSP's main fund reports $335M sold (BSP firm profile).

Gaps

  • The context names no rivals for Bully Pulpit International or Fair Harbor. A sponsor deal log for comms/public affairs and consumer apparel would close this gap.
  • Calibre Scientific's sponsor is not identified.
  • Fund sizes for some peers are unknown (Private-equity landscape).

Next actions

  1. Build a proprietary outreach list of PA/NJ shops below $3M EBITDA for Punctual Pros. Use the franchise-system angle rather than join auctions.
  2. Track Horizon and Heartland as possible asset sellers. Heartland's debt matures Dec 15, 2026.
  3. Speed up CET's New England electrical, wastewater and energy-efficiency add-on pipeline. Set alerts on Albireo and Kohlberg deals in the region.
  4. Commission sponsor-activity scans for the comms/public affairs and apparel sectors so Bully Pulpit International and Fair Harbor are covered.
